o: For each cap x from 1 to n, replace every element > x with x, and decide whether some subsequence sums to exactly k. Example 1 (nums=[4,3,2,4], k=5): x=1,2 fail; x=3,4 succeed via 2+3. Brute force rebuilds a knapsack per x — O(n²k), too slow at n=k=4000. The fix: elements ≤ x are identical to the originals, so one incrementally-built knapsack serves all x.
k: Under cap x, elements split into 'unchanged' (value ≤ x) and 'capped' (value > x, all equal to x).
Build the subset-sum DP over unchanged elements incrementally as x grows: when advancing to x, insert all elements equal to x.
Then the answer for x is: exists t ≥ 0 with t·x ≤ k, t ≤ (#elements > x), and dp[k − t·x] true. Since t ≤ k/x, the t-loop totals O(k log n) across all x.

a.n: Approach 1: Rebuild Knapsack per x (Conceptual Baseline)
a.i: For each x, cap the array and run a fresh O(n·k) subset-sum. Correct but O(n²·k) ≈ 6.4·10¹⁰ operations — far too slow; included to motivate the incremental design.
s: For each x in 1..n, build capped = [min(v, x) for v in nums].
Run standard 0/1 knapsack up to k.
a.t: O(n² · k) — infeasible at the given constraints; baseline only.

a.n: Approach 2: Incremental Knapsack + Bounded Cap Counting (Optimal)
a.i: Maintain dp over elements with value ≤ current x (identical to their capped selves), updated once per distinct value. Capped elements all equal x, so trying t = 0, 1, …, min(count>x, k/x) of them covers every combination. Total work: O(n·k) for the DP plus O(k log n) for all t-loops.
s: Sweep x = 1..n: first add all elements equal to x into the knapsack (descending-sum 0/1 update), decrementing the '> x' counter.
For each x, scan t from 0 while t·x ≤ k and t ≤ countGreaterThanX; success if dp[k − t·x].
a.t: O(n·k + k log n) — the knapsack is built once incrementally; the geometric t-loop sum is harmonic.
a.sp: O(n + k) for counts and the DP array.

w: The decomposition 'unchanged elements + t copies of the cap' is the whole problem — recognize that capped elements collapse to a single repeated value. Pitfalls: rebuilding the DP per x (TLE), forgetting the bound t ≤ (number of elements > x), and DP update direction (descending sums for 0/1 semantics). Follow-up: return the actual subsequence, or handle caps beyond n / k up to 1e9 with bitset DP.
